principles: Flag OFF => byte-identical dispatch (the cardinal safety invariant)
One-way seam: dispatch -> ledger; usage-ledger keeps zero cross-module imports
Complex logic lives as PURE testable functions in-module; the dispatch edit is a minimal gated call
Defensive: parse-failure falls back to raw text + unavailable; ledger errors caught; never break dispatch
provider-reported final supersedes the preflight estimate (no double count); claude-host-only real usage now
drivers: User authorized touching dispatch to record REAL token counts per story
Editing the core dispatch path is high-risk and must be bounded by hard invariants
Lattice never sees host usage unless it requests + parses structured host output

options.name: A: pure in-module orchestrator + parser + a minimal gated seam in lattice-dispatch.ts
B: inline all estimate/parse/record logic directly in lattice-dispatch.ts
cons: Bloats + risks the hot dispatch path; hard to unit-test; couples dispatch to ledger internals — rejected

options.name: C: estimate-only seam (no real usage)
cons: Does not deliver real numbers — declined by the user

chosen: A: pure in-module orchestrator + parser + a minimal gated seam in lattice-dispatch.ts
rationale: Putting the estimate/parse/record logic in pure in-module functions keeps it fully unit-testable and keeps the dispatch edit a minimal, flag-gated call, so the high-risk core-path change is bounded: OFF is byte-identical and the only live failure modes (unparseable output, ledger error) degrade safely to today's behavior.

preMortem.scenario: Flag OFF silently changes dispatch behavior (regression on the core path)
preMortem.mitigation: Keep the disabled path's spawn args ['--print', promptFile] + raw-stdout handling literally unchanged; CHK-004 asserts OFF is byte-identical (arg-builder + result text)

preMortem.scenario: --output-format json breaks the downstream result text
preMortem.trigger: stdout becomes JSON, downstream expects raw text
preMortem.consequence: Dispatch result corrupted when ledger ON
preMortem.mitigation: Parser extracts .result as the text used downstream; on parse failure fall back to raw stdout; only when flag ON; CHK-002/CHK-004 test both

preMortem.scenario: A ledger error throws and breaks a real dispatch
preMortem.consequence: Real work fails because of diagnostics
preMortem.mitigation: All ledger work in try/catch; recordDispatch* swallow internally and never throw to the caller; CHK-001 tests

preMortem.scenario: provider-reported final double-counts with the preflight estimate
preMortem.mitigation: Final lists the estimate recordId in supersedesRecordIds; summary excludes superseded; CHK-005 simulated end-to-end asserts story total counts only the final

preMortem.scenario: usage-ledger gains a cross-module import (dispatch types)
preMortem.mitigation: Orchestrator/parser take plain inputs (no dispatch import); dispatch does the mapping; smoke asserts usage-ledger imports zero other modules

preMortem.scenario: Claude CLI JSON shape/flag assumption is wrong for the installed version
preMortem.consequence: Usage not parsed / dispatch text wrong
preMortem.mitigation: Defensive parse, raw-text fallback + unavailable on any mismatch; never assume; documented; OFF unaffected
